headline: The product excluding i is the product strictly to its left times the product strictly to its right
statement: Return an array whose i-th value is the product of every nums element except nums[i]. Use O(n) time without division. Products of all prefixes and suffixes fit signed 32-bit integers. Use constant auxiliary space excluding the returned array.
intuition: For each position, multiply everything before it by everything after it. First make a forward pass to save the product on the left. Then make a backward pass to multiply in the product on the right. Excluding the current value happens naturally, without division or special handling for zero.
approach: Fill result[i] with the running product before including nums[i].
Scan backwards with a suffix product initially 1.
Multiply result[i] by the suffix, then include nums[i] in the suffix.
correctness: The first pass stores exactly the product of indices below i. The reverse pass carries exactly the product of indices above i. Their product covers every index except i exactly once; empty sides contribute the identity 1.
bruteForce: For each index multiply every other element: O(n²) time.

complexity.explanation: Two linear scans reuse the returned array for left products. Only the scalar prefix and suffix products and loop indices occupy additional storage; the n output entries are excluded.

pitfalls: Update running products after writing the current index.
One zero differs from two zeros; the two-pass method handles both automatically.
Division violates the requirement and fails at zero.
